'''Janu Godalhi''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[lawyer]] and security expert who worked with [[Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon]] to drive [[pirate]]s from the [[planet]] [[Teth]]. In [[19 BBY]], he attended a showing of the [[opera]] ''[[Squid Lake]]'' at the [[Galaxies Opera House]] on the planet [[Coruscant]].

After the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Janu Godalhi became leader of a group of rebels who opposed the Empire on Teth. He worked closely with [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] members [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] and later [[Mon Mothma]].

==Biography==
Janu Godalhi was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]]<ref name="VE">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref> who worked as an [[lawyer]] and security expert. At some point prior to the [[Clone Wars]], he worked with [[Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon]] to rid the [[Wild Space]] [[planet]] [[Teth]] of a group of [[pirate]]s, which also ended up driving the last [[Hutt]]s from the world as well.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

During the Clone Wars between the [[Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> in [[19 BBY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of {{Film|III}} to [[19 BBY]].</ref> Godalhi attended a performance<ref name="ROTS" /> of the [[opera]] ''[[Squid Lake]]'' at the [[Galaxies Opera House]] in the [[Uscru District]] of the planet [[Coruscant]].<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> While at the opera, he walked through a corridor behind the floor level seating.<ref name="ROTS" />

Not long after the performance, [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] issued [[Order 66]] and declared the [[Jedi Order]] traitors, leading to the [[Death|execution]] of many [[Jedi]] including Koon.<ref name="ROTS" /> Godalhi never believed Palpatine's claims about the Jedi, and following the Republic's [[Proclamation of the New Order|transition]] into the [[Galactic Empire]], Godalhi became the [[Janu Godalhi's rebel group|leader of one]] of the two rebel groups active on Teth who were opposing the Empire. He worked closely with [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] and later [[Mon Mothma]], members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]], and continued to hinder the Empire.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> He shared his surname<ref name="VE" /> with [[DJ (occupation)|radio DJ]] [[Palob Godalhi]].<ref name="Batuu">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge: Traveler's Guide to Batuu]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Godalhi was an energetic<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> individual with light skin and brown [[hair]].<ref name="VE" />

==Equipment==
While at the opera, Godalhi wore a [[Color|green]] [[cloak]] with a [[Clothing|hoopskirt]] hem and a matching [[hat]].<ref name="VE" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|It was a heavy green dress with a hoop-skirt hem and an upholstered finish that made me feel not unlike a 1970s sofa, shaped like a playing piece from the classic "Sorry" board-game. Just add a strange hat, and you're set.|Pablo Hidalgo|<ref name="Hyp">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/postnotes/news20041124.html|series=Episode III Post Notes|text=Part of the Coruscant Elite}}</ref>}}
Janu Godalhi was portrayed in a cameo by [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]]<ref name="Hyp" /> in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']],<ref name="ROTS" /> which was released on [[May 19]], [[2005]].<ref name="YbY">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> Despite only being fleetingly visible in the film, Hidalgo had to wear contact lenses for the role as director [[George Lucas]] did not want any eyeglasses to appear.<ref name="Hyp" />

Hidlago was filmed as Godalhi on [[November 17]], [[2004]] at [[Industrial Light & Magic]] in two different shots starting at 3pm. In the first shot, Hidlago was stood in the hallway outside the theater auditorium with ILM staff members [[Katherine Farrar]], [[Lars Jensvold]], and [[David Gray]]. The group talked before heading through a doorway to take their seats;<ref name="Hyp" /> however, this shot was not used in the final cut of the film.<ref name="ROTS" /> Hidalgo's solo shot, which did make it into the film, was the final shot of the day. He was filmed walking a slightly curving line marked by three masking tape crosses on the floor. While walking away from camera he looked over his left shoulder to glance at the performance, while walking toward camera he had to glance over his right shoulder.<ref name="Hyp" />

In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the character was first identified in an episode of ''[[The Star Wars Show]]'' released on [[Wikipedia:YouTube|YouTube]] on [[July 6]], [[2016]].<ref name="SWShow">{{StarWarsShow|zkwWqSx5NgA|Celebration Live Stream Announce, Black Series Fan Vote, and Lizzie Armanto|sw_url=video/the-star-wars-show-episode-9}}</ref> The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was created by users [[Adrick Tolliver]], "[[gohan316427]]," and "[[General Tarfful]]" in an entry for the [[What's The Story?]] feature of [[StarWars.com]] that was published to the [[Databank (original)|Databank]]<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|janugodalhi|Godalhi, Janu}}</ref> on [[August 12]], 2005.<ref name="DatabankDate">{{SWArchive|url=databank/updates/news20050812.html|text=Hyperspace Presents: What's the Story, Round 1}}</ref> The entry established [[Janu Godalhi/Legends|Janu Godalhi]] to be the [[Parent/Legends|father]] of [[Palob Godalhi/Legends|Palob Godalhi]],<ref name="DB" /> a pre-existing character from the [[1998]] novel ''[[Rebel Dawn]]'' by [[A. C. Crispin]].<ref name="RD">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref>
